[round 1, 8a7daa17] Reproduced. On this page's courses table, 'WHERE credits = 3 ORDER BY fee DESC, course_id' returns 103 (NULL fee) before 101 (120.00), so the keyed answer to 'highest fee first' lists the unpriced course first, the exact trap Activity 3 teaches. The NULL ordering is the simulator's, and it matches the cited documentation default; no server was run. The critic's second option ('state every 3-credit course has a fee') contradicts the page's own table, so the required fix is the first: make the keyed option 'WHERE credits = 3 ORDER BY fee DESC NULLS LAST, course_id;'. Then update its why/okNote in src/filtering-and-sorting.topic.js, the 'Question, with its answer' static block, artifact.md, and the distractor d text and feedback so it still differs only by the tie-breaker. This rewords the content of the apply item. The apply mechanics do not change.

[round 1, 8a7daa17] Reproduced. 'ORDER BY 3, 1 DESC' in Activity 2 returns the right order but gets 'your ORDER BY does not say city first ... so that order is not promised', which is false, because output-column numbers are valid sort keys (cited documentation). 'ORDER BY fee DESC NULLS LAST, 1' in Activity 3 gets 'nothing breaks a tie', although column 1 is course_id. SQLCHK.orderCols in authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/controller.js reads only k.e.col. Acceptable fix: map an integer literal k to the k-th select item's column, and an output alias to its expression, before comparing. This loosens what completes the activities, but it corrects the per-activity query check, not the attempt, retry or credit rules that the captain decision covers. If the task owner reads the constraint as covering check criteria, use the critic's fallback: keep the criterion and reword the notes to ask for column names ('name the sort columns instead of their numbers') without claiming the order is not promised. A note that calls a promised order unpromised must not ship.

[round 1, 8a7daa17] Verified. Every unreadable statement, the empty-file prompt and every real subset limit reach the shell as kind 'limit' from the adapter's check() in authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/engine.js; I reproduced 'SELEC * FROM students;', a missing comma between two VALUES rows, a missing semicolon before a second SELECT and the untouched starter, all kind 'limit'. authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/controller.js relabels 'limit' as 'Not in this practice editor', and LIMITS item 4 in authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/build.mjs plus every page's Sources footer ('not as invalid PostgreSQL') say that label never means the SQL is wrong. The label is page-owned, so it is fixable in scope. Acceptable fix: in controller.js, wrap EDITOR.check (EDITOR is Object.create of the adapter) and re-kind problems by message into three classes. Real subset limits (WITH, psql meta-commands, CREATE TABLE and so on) keep 'Not in this practice editor'. Unreadable statements ('could not read the statement near', 'could not read one starting') get a learner label such as 'Check your SQL'. The empty-file prompt gets its own neutral label. Message matching is feasible: I checked that real limits carry their own messages ('WITH queries are outside this practice editor', 'CREATE is not available here', 'Transactions are outside this practice editor', 'COPY runs on the database server', and the psql meta-command text), distinct from the unreadable-statement messages. Never use the adapter's own 'Lesson check' (B4), and never use kind 'hint', because the shell blocks Run only on non-hint problems. Run gating, the 'limit' notRun status and onSqlRun's 'did not use up a try' path must stay exactly as they are (E2 is pending). Reword LIMITS item 4 and the footer sentence in each src/<topic>.body.html and artifact.md to match. The minimum acceptable fix, if message matching seems too brittle, is one neutral label covering both cases, with LIMITS and footer sentences that no longer say the SQL is fine. Shell wording stays a recipe finding.

[round 1, 8a7daa17] Reproduced at 570x1000 under file:// and over http://127.0.0.1: scrollY 157, exactly the top of #activity-1. At 1280 px it is 121 on inner-and-left-joins and 0 where the document fits. Cause confirmed: with history.replaceState stubbed out, scrollY stays 0. The last line of authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/controller.js calls go(...,'replace'), whose history.replaceState(#activity-1) runs during parsing. It does not throw, and the browser's load-time scroll-to-fragment then scrolls to #activity-1, so F1 fails on the narrow frame (G7). Fix in controller.js: on first load with no #activity-N in the URL, do not write a hash (call go with no history mode), or write it after load and keep scroll at 0. Keep the hash behaviour for later navigation. Measured in headless Chromium only; check the platform embed after the fix.

[round 2, f18bccaf] Verified at f18bccaf. Loop 1 (for the shared E1/F5 Problems-label finding) added EDITOR.check in authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/controller.js. It re-kinds every adapter 'limit' whose message is not on a phrase list as kind 'error' (shown as 'Error'). Replayed with the adapter's check() and that exact regex: SELECT * FROM public.students; ... ORDER BY name COLLATE "C"; UPDATE students SET (city, name) = (...); SELECT DATE '2024-01-01'; and ORDER BY student_id USING > all become Error. These are valid PostgreSQL per the cited SELECT, UPDATE and lexical-structure documentation (not executed on a server). The adapter's generic messages ('could not read the statement near', 'Expected ... near', 'The statement ends too early') cannot tell a real mistake from unsupported valid syntax. The rule in DESIGN.md (Editor workspace, Problems: "An error the real language certainly raises is danger. An unsupported construct ('limit') is warning") and in authoring/evidence/python/python-fundamentals/lesson-editor/README.md (adapter contract: kind "error" is reserved for code the real language certainly rejects) therefore forbids this relabelling. The fix also missed its own target: the typo 'SELEC * FROM students;' still comes back as a limit. Remedy (a), REVERT: remove the loop-1 EDITOR.check override (and its comment), restoring the 8a7daa17 behaviour where every adapter 'limit' shows as 'Not in this practice editor'. That matches the unchanged LIMITS item 4 in build.mjs ("Anything else is marked Not in this practice editor: a limit of this page, not a sign that your SQL is wrong") and the page footers again. Run gating is unaffected either way: the shell blocks Run on any non-hint problem, and onSqlRun's 'did not use up a try' path is unchanged. Keep the separate loop-1 E5 wording in onSqlRun ('a missing comma or semicolon is often at the end of the line before it'); it does not depend on the override. This REOPENS the shared E1/F5 Problems-label finding on all eight pages (C2E-AGG-03, C2E-ANTI-03, C2E-FILT-06, C2E-GRP-04, C2E-NULL-02, C2E-JOIN-05, C2E-IUD-02 (graded high), C2E-SEED-01): real mistakes are again labelled 'Not in this practice editor', which the LIMITS text says is not a sign of wrong SQL. Record it as a recipe finding for the sql-practice adapter in authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/engine.js. The adapter should give kind 'error' only to statements it can prove malformed (an unclosed quote or bracket, a statement ending after WHERE/AND) and give generic parse failures neutral wording ('could not read this; check for a typo, or it may be SQL this editor does not support'). Until then, this is an open item for the task owner. Remedy (b), leave, is rejected: it tells learners valid SQL is wrong, in breach of the adapter contract.

[round 3, 02be5a14] Verified at 02be5a14 by parsing the bank with authoring/tools/gift/validate.mjs parseGift and comparing option answer lengths (correct vs longest distractor): 'o1 AND before OR' 47 vs 39; 'o3 no ORDER BY' 54 vs 40; 'o3 stable ties' 30 vs 26. Is the remedy available on this branch? No. In authoring/tests/gift-answer-order.test.mjs, the test 'topic GIFT banks keep the semantics they had before the answer-order permutation' parses each bank at baseline f2647727 (present in this clone, so the test is not skipped). For every baseline question, baselineProblems() reports '<title> changed' when semanticDigest differs. In authoring/tools/gift/answer-order.mjs, semanticDigest hashes the category, the title, the stem and each option's [correct, answer, feedback] text. So any wording change that lengthens a distractor or trims a correct option changes the digest and fails npm test. This bank exists at the baseline. Its bytes at 02be5a14 are identical to origin/main (sha256 compared), so the length cue is pre-existing on main and not introduced by this branch's content. The only edit the test allows is appending new questions with new titles. That cannot remove the cue from the existing items, so it is not a fix. Decision: escalate, not reject, because the finding is true and fails C2 D7 ('the correct option is not the longest') and DESIGN.md Assessment. It cannot be accepted on this branch, because the only remedy needs a test or tooling change, which the branch may not make. The captain or tooling owner must decide whether to refresh the frozen baseline for reviewed wording-only length rebalancing, or to add a reviewed-exception mechanism. That would be a tooling branch, followed by a course or module branch that rebalances these items with answer-order.mjs, keeping each option's meaning and the keyed answer.
